quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog and slow down. If fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Change in direction ahead.
School zone and crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are leaving a divided highway and entering a road with traffic going both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What type of headlights should you use in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder for you to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn is allowed here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may proceed. First, check that the intersection is clear and yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in it.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking on a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: What should you do when a child on a bicycle is near your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable and make sudden changes in direction. Bicycles are also small and hard to see, so be extra careful.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
When the yellow line next to your side is broken.
When the yellow line next to the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line next to your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the merging lane to speed up and match the speed of traffic already on the interstate. Then merge smoothly when it is safe. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway?

options.text: Stop only if people are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect people on the sidewalk to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down and give the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?

options.text: When you drive a few mph faster than most other vehicles.
When you stay within that speed range.
When you drive a few mph slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic around you. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Accidents often happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: You must stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended arm. Stay stopped until the arm is pulled back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are going the same direction or the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School zone or crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers about a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car merges too close in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space without requiring hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: What problems can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Loss of vehicle control.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of vehicle control.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do when you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zones have signs warning of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange warning signs.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back to the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Keep your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: The truck may complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
The truck must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may need to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels of a vehicle follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need to swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes moving in your direction, and many vehicles are passing you on the right. If a driver behind you wants to drive faster, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance and show it to an officer after any traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: What is a distraction while driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what documents must you have?

options.text: Only insurance and registration.
Only your driver's license.
Your license, insurance, and registration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license, insurance, and registration.
questions.explanation: You must produce your license, registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. All three documents must be in your vehicle while driving.

questions.question: When a cyclist is turning left, what may they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Expect to see cyclists riding with traffic. Do not be surprised if a cyclist uses the left lane to turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign is a traffic law. Where this sign is posted, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped in your lane with red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop while the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop while the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When involved in a crash, what should you do with injured people?

options.text: Do not move them unless you must.
Move them where they want to go.
Tell them they are fine and do not need medical help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless you must.
questions.explanation: Moving injured people can make injuries worse. Only move someone if there is danger like fire. Keep injured people sitting or lying down until medical help arrives.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights and a siren, you must pull over to the side and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: After a train passes a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train on any track. Do not move until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the proper lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the proper lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in the correct lane for a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow when it is safe. This is true whether the arrow is alone or with other signals.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken line next to a solid line means traffic in the lane next to the broken line may pass. Traffic in the lane next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: What are "no zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and move safely.
Areas where cars have enough space behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and move safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars cannot be seen by the truck driver or are so close that they limit the truck's ability to stop and turn safely. A car in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make stopping distances longer and crashes more severe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where a crosswalk is located. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before turning.
When traffic moves to the right.
When traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.
